newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures end mixed in choppy session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures end mixed in choppy session.

text.p: NYMEX California-Oregon Border (COB) electricity futures settled higher Friday, while the Palo Verde (PV) half of the complex ended lower in a choppy session.
"It popped back up because gas is holding. You're seeing a lot of short-covering," said a Houston futures trader.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natural gas futures finished up 30 cents at $2.824 per million British thermal units (mmBtu) after hitting a low of $2.655.
February gas deliveries to San Juan/Blanco Hub ended at $2.45-$2.50/mmBtu, up from Thursday's $2.30-$2.35.
The complex reflected today's divergence in the underlying cash activity in the West, where prices at COB weakened and those at PV held steady.

Monday between 0630 and 1800 PDT, southbound transmissions on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie were limited to 2,000 megawatts (MW), compared with a usual rating of 3,200 MW, for planned maintenance work.
February California-Oregon Border (COB) settled down 32 cents at $13.91 a megawatt hour (MWh) after bouncing between $13.65 and $14.35.
March COB ended at $11.65, down 26 cents. Other active COB contracts finished 10 to 30 cents lower.
February Palo Verde (PV) futures settled up 52 cents at $16.60, its session high. Most PV deferreds were inactive.
Forcasts indicated coastal rain and mountain snow would fall across most of the Northwest today and temperatures would run near to slightly below normal through the weekend.
In the Southwest, temperatures would average four to eight degrees F above normal through the weekend, with chance of showers along the coast and interior California, and snow in the mountains.
Separately, a 750 megawatt (MW) power turbine at the Grand Coulee hydroelectric dam in Washington state is expected to resume operation Monday after being shut for unplanned repairs Tuesday.
A 500 kilvolt transmission line, which runs from Snohomish County, Wash. to the Canadian border, could be restored to service Monday after damage from an ice storm last week.

The outage of the 350 megawatt (MW) unit 1 at the Comanche coal-fired power plant in Pueblo, Colorado, was extended to middle of next week as more time was needed to repair damages from a fire in mid-December.
The refueling outage of the 1,070 MW unit 2 at the San Onofre nuclear power plant is said to be extended into mid-February.
